as_told.title: JC says he is from Office of Naval Intelligence and offers slow drip disclosure deal

plain: In 1996, a stranger calling himself JC is said to have turned up at a party at the Los Angeles home of Bryce Zabel, co-creator of Dark Skies, a TV series about a government cover-up of aliens. He claimed to have seen the show's first episode before it aired. Zabel tells it himself: JC wanted "to congratulate me on a successful show" and said, "You guys got a lot right." Brent Friedman, a writer on the series who was there, adds that JC said he was from the Office of Naval Intelligence, the Navy's spy service, and offered them access to information if they would help with a "slow drip disclosure program," a gradual release of the truth about aliens to the public. If true, a military intelligence office was trying to use Hollywood to prepare people for that truth.
